Each transition consumes one step, so u2 is reached exactly when has_door_key is true on two distinct moves, and any two holding moves drive u0->u1->u2; sound and complete. Consecutive holding steps (pickup, then any non-drop move) count as two different moves, which matches the literal wording — the task counts moves on which the agent holds the key and does not demand a drop between them, so no fourth state with an intervening non-holding requirement is needed. REACHABILITY: all states reachable — the key spawns in the start room, so pickup makes has_door_key true (u0->u1), and one further holding move or a drop-and-repick reaches u2. COMPACTNESS: 3 states is minimal for counting to two. PREDICATE-ONLY/ELSE COVERAGE: labels are single propositions; every state has an else self-loop, so the irrelevant propositions door_open and target_picked_up and the sole event key_lost are correctly subsumed; key_lost is rightly unused (it would even misfire on the post-door_open drop). PERSISTENT/EVENT DISTINCTION: has_door_key is a condition used as a per-step guard, appropriate here. REGRESSIONS: none required — the count is monotone because has_door_key turning false cannot erase past holding moves, and the u1 else self-loop preserves the count through drops. REWARD SAFETY: dense (0.2 at the first holding move), ordered (0.2 < 1.0), bounded and unfarmable — u2 is absorbing via its else self-loop (has_door_key in u2 falls through to else), each rewarding transition fires at most once, max total 1.2. FORMAT: nonempty FINAL_STATES (u2), u2 declared in STATES and accepting exactly when the task is satisfied, INITIAL_STATE declared, zero-reward else transitions correctly omitted by convention. No violations found.

feedback:
Accepted. The candidate defines exactly the four environment-declared propositions and no extras, and each matches its documented truth condition.

has_door_key: persistent current-state condition. Returns true only when env.carrying is a key and some door in the grid has the same color, exactly matching the documented expression. The None guards (carrying is not None, c is not None before attribute reads) prevent runtime errors, and the genexp scan over env.width x env.height via env.grid.get is within the documented API. Correct for the RM's (u0, has_door_key) -> u1 and (u1, has_door_key) -> u2 edges: it is true on every step the key is held, so holding it on two distinct moves drives u0 -> u1 -> u2.

door_open: persistent, reads c.is_open on the single door each step, so it can turn false again by a closing toggle, matching the environment semantics. Exact match to the documented expression.

target_picked_up: persistent, checks the carried object is a box and that env.mission equals f"pick up the {env.carrying.color} box", matching the designated box via the mission string rather than assuming a fixed color. Exact match to the documented expression; the last-step-only aspect is enforced by the environment terminating, not the labeler.

key_lost: correctly implemented as an event with the documented reading prev["has_door_key"] and not K and not D. It reads env.episode_memory["previous_valuation"] read-only, compares the current has_door_key and door_open expressions (inlined identically to the standalone functions) against that snapshot, and mutates nothing. The guard on previous_valuation's truthiness is redundant given a complete valuation is always supplied but is harmless and preserves the required first-step falsity. The not D conjunct correctly prevents key_lost from firing on the post-open drop, and the not K conjunct keeps it disjoint from has_door_key.

No imports, no actions, no side effects, no mutation of the environment or episode memory. Syntax is valid executable Python. No declared predicate is missing and no undeclared function is present; the RM's else edges require no labeling support.
